interface.title: Paper Section Extractor
interface.field: Scientific literature processing / document parsing for retrieval (RAG) pipelines
interface.stage_of_work: Preparing source papers: splitting a paper into sections before reading it, retrieving from it, or handing it to an LLM
interface.what_it_is_for: Upload a scientific paper PDF and get back its detected sections (Abstract, numbered sections and subsections, Methods, Results, References and so on), each with its page range and text, with an optional keyword filter over section titles and content.

data.note: I uploaded sample_paper.pdf (3.5 KB, one page). It gives 10 sections: Abstract, 1. Introduction, Related Work, 2. Methods, 2.1 Data Collection, 2.2 Header Detection, 3. Results, 4. Discussion, 5. Conclusion, References. Every section shows 'pages 1–1', so this file cannot test page ranges that span pages. The tool has no built-in example.

features.name: Collapsible outline of document sections with page ranges
features.general: Show a document as a list of headings, each labelled with the pages it covers. Open a heading to read its text and close it again, so you can check each part on its own.
features.specific: The Extracted Sections panel shows one '📘 <title> · pages a–b' row per detected section. Clicking a row opens it to show that section's paragraphs in order. Clicking again closes it. Several rows can be open at once. Only one-page ranges ('pages 1–1') were seen; ranges that cross a page break are untested.
steps: Run the extraction to fill the list
Read the section titles and page ranges
Click a section row to open its text
Open more rows to compare where neighbouring sections start and end
Click an open row to close it
serves_tasks: Open one section and read its text with its page range
Check that subsections, the reference list and the other sections were split at the right places
Copy the text of one section to give it to an LLM

features.name: Keyword filter applied when the extraction runs
features.general: Type a word or phrase, re-run the processing, and keep only the parts whose heading or body contains it. Matching ignores letter case and finds the text anywhere inside a word or sentence. A count of the kept parts is reported.
features.specific: Type into Search sections, then press 🚀 Extract Sections. The section list shrinks to sections whose title or content contains the query, and the status reads '✅ Extracted N sections.' Matching ignores case ('results' matches '3. Results') and accepts multi-word phrases ('section boundaries'). It matches text only, not the section hierarchy, so a parent heading does not bring its subsections. Typing alone or pressing Enter does nothing. A query with no match gives '✅ Extracted 0 sections.' and an empty panel with no message. Leaving the box empty brings back all sections.
steps: Type a query in Search sections
Read the match count in the status line
Open the matching sections to see where the query appears
Clear the box and extract again to see every section
serves_tasks: Find the sections whose body text mentions a word
Narrow the paper down to its methods section
Find every section that discusses a topic named by a phrase

features.name: PDF upload with run status and progress
features.general: Drop in a single document, start processing, watch progress, and get a one-line summary of the result.
features.specific: The Upload PDF box accepts one .pdf and shows its name, its size and a download link back to the file, with an × to clear it. 🚀 Extract Sections shows a 'Running pipeline...' progress bar, then '✅ Extracted N sections.' Pressing it with no file shows red Error badges and leaves the old results on screen; this is a handler bug (on_extract returns 5 values for 6 outputs, app.py:67), not designed error handling, and the intended '⚠️ Upload a PDF first.' message never appears.
steps: Click Click to Upload and choose a PDF
Press 🚀 Extract Sections and watch the progress bar
Clear the file with × to start over
serves_tasks: Load a paper and split it into sections with page ranges

The server writes outputs/extracted_sections.md/.json, but the UI offers no way to get them, so the hand-off stage is limited to copying text by hand.

Browse page provenance for a single paragraph: the interface shows page ranges per section only ('pages 1–1'), not per paragraph. Also, sample_paper.pdf has one page, so I could not check sections that span pages.

Search for 'dataset', 'evaluation' and 'evaluation metrics' (the README's examples): all found 0 sections ('dataset': screens/013.webp; 'evaluation': screens/026.webp), because the sample paper does not use those words. Typing 'dataset' and pressing Enter changed nothing (screens/010.webp, screens/011.webp). Search itself works (see 'papers', 'Methods', 'section boundaries').

Isolate Methods together with its subsections: searching 'Methods' returned 2. Methods and 2.2 Header Detection but not 2.1 Data Collection. The search matches text, not the section hierarchy, so I took Methods alone by opening it and copying its text.

See what Debug mode does: ticking Debug mode and extracting gave the same 10 sections and no visible change (screens/019.webp, screens/021.webp, screens/022.webp), because the Debug Output box is created hidden (app.py:167).

Run without a document: pressing 🚀 Extract Sections with an empty upload box (screens/002.webp) or after clearing the file with × (screens/028.webp) gave red Error badges and left earlier results on screen. This is a crash in on_extract (5 return values for 6 outputs, app.py:67), not designed error handling.
